categories.name: Vision-Language-Action
categories.blurb: End-to-end models that map camera images + a language instruction directly to robot actions, usually built on a pretrained VLM backbone.

categories.name: Imitation Learning & Policies
categories.blurb: Learning manipulation from human demonstrations: behavior cloning, action chunking, diffusion and flow-matching policies.

categories.name: Reinforcement Learning
categories.blurb: Policies improved from reward and interaction — online, offline, sim-to-real, and human-in-the-loop.

categories.name: World Models & Dreaming
categories.blurb: Learned predictive models of the environment used for planning or for training policies inside imagination.

categories.name: World Action Models
categories.blurb: Policies whose backbone is a generative model of the future: video or latent prediction and action decoding trained under one objective, so the dynamics model *is* the policy rather than a module beside it.

categories.name: VLM / LLM Planning & Grounding
categories.blurb: Using foundation models as the high-level reasoner: task decomposition, affordance grounding, code generation, keypoint selection.

categories.name: Representations & Architectures
categories.blurb: The substrate: backbone architectures, visual pretraining, 3D scene representations and action tokenizers.

categories.name: Robot Datasets & Collection
categories.blurb: The fuel: large-scale real robot trajectory corpora, the interfaces used to collect them, and the methods that multiply a few demonstrations into many.

categories.name: Benchmarks & Evaluation
categories.blurb: The yardstick: simulated task suites, evaluation protocols, and the studies that check whether reported gains survive contact with statistics.

categories.name: Human Data & Egocentric Video
categories.blurb: Learning manipulation from people rather than robots: egocentric video, wearable capture, hand tracking, and the latent-action and co-training methods that convert action-free human footage into robot supervision.

categories.name: Simulation & Sim2Real
categories.blurb: Physics engines, massively parallel simulation, and the randomization tricks that let sim-trained policies survive reality.

technologies.name: GEN-1.5
technologies.tagline: A 3-second clip in the context window is the whole training procedure.

technologies.name: Skild S1
technologies.tagline: Show it one human video and it does the task — no fine-tuning, no demonstrations on the robot.

technologies.name: Spirit v1.5 / v1.6
technologies.full_name: Spirit v1.5 / v1.6: A Robotic Foundation Model by Spirit AI
technologies.tagline: First Chinese model to top RoboArena, beating both of NVIDIA's entries on their own leaderboard.

technologies.name: Gemini Robotics 2
technologies.tagline: Gemini stops being a pair of arms: one VLA that walks, crouches and manipulates as a single coordinated body.

technologies.name: RoboDojo
technologies.full_name: RoboDojo: A Unified Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Comprehensive Evaluation of Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies
technologies.tagline: One evaluation layer spanning 42 simulated and 18 real tasks, with the real robots rented out so results reproduce.

technologies.name: AgiBot GO-2
technologies.tagline: Chain-of-thought over actions, not words, to keep long-horizon plans from drifting apart from execution.

technologies.name: pi-0.7
technologies.full_name: pi-0.7: a Steerable Model with Emergent Capabilities
technologies.tagline: Train on prompts that say how, not just what — and per-task RL fine-tuning stops being necessary.

technologies.name: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory (MEM)
technologies.full_name: VLAs with Long and Short-Term Memory
technologies.tagline: A VLA that remembers what it already did, so tasks can run past ten minutes without losing the thread.

technologies.name: RL Token / efficient online RL
technologies.full_name: Precise Manipulation with Efficient Online RL
technologies.tagline: Extract one RL token from a frozen VLA and you can run online reinforcement learning on it in hours, not weeks.

technologies.name: DreamZero
technologies.full_name: World Action Models are Zero-shot Policies
technologies.tagline: Make the video model the policy: denoise future frames and actions in one transformer, and control comes out zero-shot.

technologies.name: MolmoSpaces
technologies.full_name: MolmoSpaces: A Large-Scale Open Ecosystem for Robot Navigation and Manipulation
technologies.tagline: 230k environments built so you can vary one thing at a time — and a sim score that actually predicts the real one.

technologies.name: VLA-JEPA
technologies.full_name: VLA-JEPA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Model with Latent World Model
technologies.tagline: Predict the next state in latent space, not pixel space, so the policy learns dynamics instead of wallpaper.

technologies.name: Helix 02
technologies.tagline: Deleted the walking controller: 109,504 lines of hand-written C++ replaced by a 10M-parameter learned motion prior.

technologies.name: GR00T N2
technologies.tagline: The DreamZero architecture productized: NVIDIA's humanoid foundation model stops being a VLA and becomes a world-action model.

technologies.name: pi-*0.6 / RECAP
technologies.tagline: Let the VLA practice: RL on its own on-robot experience plus expert corrections roughly doubles throughput.

technologies.name: Dreamer 4
technologies.tagline: Train the agent entirely inside a scalable world model learned from offline data, with no environment interaction at all.

technologies.name: Gemini Robotics 1.5 / ER 1.5
technologies.tagline: Thinks before acting, and moves skills between different robot bodies without retraining.

technologies.name: Large Behavior Models
technologies.tagline: The field's most rigorous evaluation study: does multitask pretraining actually help? Yes, but less than headlines claim.

technologies.name: RoboArena
technologies.full_name: RoboArena: Distributed Real-World Evaluation of Generalist Robot Policies
technologies.tagline: Stop arguing about cherry-picked demos: rank policies by double-blind pairwise duels run on other people's robots.

technologies.name: SmolVLA
technologies.tagline: A 450M VLA trained only on community-contributed datasets that runs on a laptop.

technologies.name: V-JEPA 2
technologies.tagline: Predict in representation space, not pixels, then plan with the result using only tens of hours of robot data.

technologies.name: EgoDex
technologies.tagline: Hundreds of hours of egocentric dexterous manipulation with 3D hand and finger tracking already attached.

technologies.name: EgoZero
technologies.tagline: Train a manipulation policy from human demonstrations only — zero robot data — and deploy it.

technologies.name: GR00T N1.5
technologies.tagline: Freeze the VLM to protect grounding, and let world-model-generated dream data carry new skills.

technologies.name: pi-0.5
technologies.tagline: Cleaning entire kitchens and bedrooms it has never seen: generalization moved from new objects to new buildings.

technologies.name: AgiBot World
technologies.tagline: A million-plus bimanual trajectories collected on a purpose-built humanoid fleet in staged real environments.

technologies.name: Gemini Robotics / Robotics-ER
technologies.tagline: Gemini itself, taught to act, plus a sibling model whose only job is spatial and physical reasoning.

technologies.name: GR00T N1
technologies.tagline: An openly released humanoid foundation model trained on a data pyramid of real, synthetic and human video.

technologies.name: Humanoid Policy ~ Human Policy (PH2D)
technologies.tagline: Collect human and humanoid data in one shared format and train a single policy over both — human data turns out to be nearly as valuable as robot data.

technologies.name: Helix
technologies.tagline: Full upper-body humanoid control at 200 Hz from onboard GPUs, with two robots collaborating under one model.

technologies.name: Hi Robot
technologies.tagline: A VLM inner monologue on top of a VLA, so you can interrupt the robot mid-task and it listens.

technologies.name: OpenVLA-OFT
technologies.tagline: Three orthogonal fixes make OpenVLA roughly 26x faster and good enough for bimanual ALOHA.

technologies.name: FAST action tokenizer
technologies.tagline: Compress action chunks with a DCT before tokenizing, which makes autoregressive VLAs viable at high control rates.

technologies.name: NVIDIA Cosmos
technologies.full_name: World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
technologies.tagline: Open world foundation models trained on tens of millions of hours of physical-world video, built as a data engine for robots.

technologies.name: SpatialVLA
technologies.tagline: Injects explicit 3D structure into a VLA, because flat image tokens throw away the geometry manipulation needs.

technologies.name: 1X World Model
technologies.tagline: Use the world model as a test harness: evaluate humanoid policies in imagination instead of on hardware.

technologies.name: CogACT
technologies.tagline: Argues the VLM should cognize and a separate diffusion module should act, then measures what that split buys.

technologies.name: ALOHA Unleashed
technologies.tagline: Scale ALOHA-style collection far enough and diffusion policies learn to tie shoelaces and hang shirts.

technologies.name: EgoMimic
technologies.tagline: Treat human data as just another embodiment and co-train on it — no retargeting stage, no separate planner.

technologies.name: GR-2
technologies.tagline: GR-1's recipe scaled to tens of millions of internet videos and 100+ real tasks.

technologies.name: HIL-SERL
technologies.tagline: Add a human who takes over when things go wrong, and RL reaches essentially perfect success on hard real tasks in a couple of hours.

technologies.name: LAPA
technologies.tagline: Invent an action space from video that has no action labels, pretrain a VLA in it, then map it onto real robot actions.

technologies.name: pi-0 (pi-zero)
technologies.full_name: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
technologies.tagline: A flow-matching action expert bolted onto a VLM, running at 50 Hz. The first VLA that could fold laundry end to end.

technologies.name: RDT-1B
technologies.tagline: The largest open diffusion policy for bimanual manipulation, with an action space built to unify incompatible robots.

technologies.name: Molmo (pointing)
technologies.tagline: An open VLM trained to point at things, which turns out to be the interface robots needed.

technologies.name: ReKep
technologies.tagline: Express manipulation as Python constraint functions over semantic keypoints, written by a VLM and solved in real time.

technologies.name: Eagle VLM backbones
technologies.tagline: The VLM backbones NVIDIA's robot models sit on: mixtures of vision encoders tuned for spatial detail.

technologies.name: Embodied Chain-of-Thought
technologies.tagline: Make the VLA write out plan, sub-task, object locations and gripper targets before acting; success jumps sharply.

technologies.name: OpenVLA
technologies.tagline: An open 7B VLA that beat the 55B RT-2-X and fine-tunes on a single consumer GPU.

technologies.name: RoboCasa
technologies.tagline: Large-scale simulated household kitchens with generatively authored scenes and thousands of objects.

technologies.name: RoboPoint
technologies.tagline: Fine-tune a VLM on synthetic spatial instruction data so it predicts exactly where to place or grasp.

technologies.name: LeRobot
technologies.tagline: The Hugging Face of robotics: one dataset format, reference policy implementations, and arms that cost a few hundred dollars.

technologies.name: Octo
technologies.tagline: The first genuinely open generalist policy designed to be fine-tuned: swap cameras, add proprioception, change the arm.

technologies.name: SIMPLER
technologies.full_name: Simulated Manipulation Policy Evaluation for Real Robot Setups
technologies.tagline: Evaluate real-robot policies in simulation, with the simulator tuned until its rankings match reality's.

technologies.name: 3D Diffusion Policy (DP3)
technologies.tagline: Swap images for a sparse point cloud and diffusion policies learn dexterous tasks from about ten demonstrations.

technologies.name: BEHAVIOR-1K
technologies.tagline: A thousand household activities chosen by surveying what people actually want robots to do, not what is convenient to simulate.

technologies.name: DROID
technologies.tagline: One hardware setup, thirteen institutions, 564 real scenes: diversity by construction rather than by aggregation.

technologies.name: MOKA
technologies.tagline: Draw candidate points on the image and ask the VLM to pick: turns motion generation into visual question answering.

technologies.name: RT-H
technologies.tagline: Insert a layer of language motions ('move arm left', 'close gripper') between the task and the actuators.

technologies.name: VQ-BeT / Behavior Transformer
technologies.tagline: Tokenize continuous actions with residual vector quantization: multimodality without diffusion's inference cost.

technologies.name: 3D Diffuser Actor
technologies.tagline: Marries 3D scene tokens with diffusion action generation, topping both RLBench and CALVIN.

technologies.name: Genie / Genie 3
technologies.tagline: Learns a latent action space from unlabeled internet video, producing worlds you can actually step through.

technologies.name: UMI
technologies.tagline: A cheap handheld gripper with an action camera: collect robot training data anywhere, with no robot.

technologies.name: Mobile ALOHA
technologies.tagline: Put ALOHA on a wheeled base, teleoperate the whole body, co-train with static data, get mobile manipulation from 50 demos.

technologies.name: SERL
technologies.tagline: A packaged software stack that trains real-robot manipulation policies from scratch in under an hour.

technologies.name: GR-1
technologies.tagline: Pretrain on large-scale human video prediction, then fine-tune the same transformer to predict actions.

technologies.name: Ego-Exo4D
technologies.tagline: Films the same skilled activity from the wearer's eyes and from outside simultaneously, so a model can learn to translate between the two.

technologies.name: Eureka
technologies.tagline: An LLM writes the reward function, evaluates how training went, and rewrites it: superhuman reward engineering.

technologies.name: MimicGen
technologies.tagline: Turn 200 human demonstrations into 50,000 by replaying object-centric segments at new object poses.

technologies.name: Open X-Embodiment
technologies.tagline: Thirty-four labs pooled their robot data into one corpus, and cross-embodiment pretraining became possible.

technologies.name: RT-X (RT-1-X / RT-2-X)
technologies.tagline: Train one policy on 22 different robots at once and each robot beats its own specialist.

technologies.name: SuSIE
technologies.tagline: Have an image-editing model hallucinate the next subgoal image, then let a cheap policy chase it.

technologies.name: TD-MPC2
technologies.tagline: Decoder-free latent model predictive control that scales to a single agent solving 104 continuous-control tasks.

technologies.name: Q-Transformer
technologies.tagline: Autoregressive Q-learning: treat each action dimension as a token and let a transformer do value-based RL at VLA scale.

technologies.name: BridgeData V2
technologies.tagline: The scrappy, diverse, low-cost dataset most open-policy research actually evaluates on.

technologies.name: Project Aria
technologies.tagline: Research glasses that turn anyone wearing them into a calibrated robot-data collector.

technologies.name: RT-2
technologies.full_name: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
technologies.tagline: Coined 'VLA': fine-tune a web-scale vision-language model to emit robot actions as text tokens, and semantic knowledge transfers to control.

technologies.name: VoxPoser
technologies.tagline: The LLM writes code that paints 3D affordance and constraint maps, and a motion planner does the rest. No robot training data.

technologies.name: LIBERO
technologies.tagline: The 130-task suite that became the default number every VLA paper reports.

technologies.name: RVT / RVT-2
technologies.tagline: Replace the expensive voxel grid with re-rendered virtual views: far faster to train and more accurate.

technologies.name: ACT / ALOHA
technologies.tagline: A cheap bimanual teleop rig plus action chunking: fine manipulation from 50 demonstrations.

technologies.name: Diffusion Policy
technologies.tagline: Generate action sequences by denoising. The single most reused idea in modern manipulation.

technologies.name: PaLM-E
technologies.tagline: Inject images and robot states directly into an LLM's token stream, and web-scale reasoning transfers to embodied tasks.

technologies.name: MimicPlay
technologies.tagline: Cheap human play video trains the high-level planner; a small amount of teleoperation trains the low-level controller.

technologies.name: RLPD
technologies.tagline: Skip offline pretraining entirely: just sample half your batch from prior data and half from online experience.

technologies.name: UniPi
technologies.full_name: Learning Universal Policies via Text-Guided Video Generation
technologies.tagline: Generate a video of the task being done, then infer the actions that produce it.

technologies.name: DreamerV3
technologies.tagline: One algorithm, one set of hyperparameters, more than 150 tasks, and the first agent to mine diamonds in Minecraft from scratch.

technologies.name: RT-1
technologies.tagline: The first convincing demonstration that one transformer, given enough real robot data, absorbs hundreds of manipulation tasks.

technologies.name: DeXtreme
technologies.tagline: Dactyl-class in-hand dexterity reproduced on a single GPU workstation instead of a compute cluster.

technologies.name: Code as Policies
technologies.tagline: Let the LLM write the policy as Python: loops, conditionals and arithmetic over perception APIs.

technologies.name: PerAct
technologies.tagline: Predict where to put the gripper in a 3D voxel grid instead of predicting joint deltas: a large sample-efficiency win.

technologies.name: Inner Monologue
technologies.tagline: Feed success detectors, scene descriptions and human replies back into the LLM so it can notice failure and replan.

technologies.name: WHIRL
technologies.tagline: Watch a person do the task once, extract a rough prior, then let the robot practise in the real world until it works.

technologies.name: DayDreamer
technologies.tagline: World models on physical robots with no simulator: a quadruped learns to walk from scratch in one hour.

technologies.name: SayCan
technologies.full_name: Do As I Can, Not As I Say
technologies.tagline: An LLM proposes what would help; learned value functions veto what the robot cannot actually do.

technologies.name: R3M
technologies.full_name: A Universal Visual Representation for Robot Manipulation
technologies.tagline: Pretrain a visual encoder on human video with time-contrastive objectives, then freeze it for robot policies.

technologies.name: BC-Z
technologies.tagline: Task-conditioned behavior cloning at scale: 100 tasks, and generalization to tasks never demonstrated.

technologies.name: CALVIN
technologies.tagline: Long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation with an explicit unseen-environment split.

technologies.name: Ego4D
technologies.tagline: Thousands of hours of daily life filmed from the wearer's own eyes — the corpus that made 'learn manipulation from human video' a real option.

technologies.name: Implicit BC
technologies.tagline: Stop regressing the action and start scoring it. Energy-based policies express discontinuity that MSE cannot.

technologies.name: Isaac Gym / Isaac Lab
technologies.tagline: Run physics and the neural network on the same GPU with thousands of environments in parallel; training times fell by orders of magnitude.

technologies.name: robomimic
technologies.tagline: The study that showed most reported gains in offline robot learning were implementation details.

technologies.name: ManiSkill / SAPIEN
technologies.tagline: Open GPU-parallel manipulation simulation with strong articulated-object support and a long-running benchmark challenge.

technologies.name: CLIP
technologies.tagline: Aligned images and text in one embedding space, which is how robots got open-vocabulary perception.

technologies.name: robosuite
technologies.tagline: The modular MuJoCo framework most academic manipulation benchmarks are built on top of.

technologies.name: CQL
technologies.tagline: Learn from a fixed dataset without the Q-function hallucinating value for actions nobody ever tried.

technologies.name: Dreamer
technologies.tagline: Stop planning at run time. Learn an actor and critic by backpropagating through thousands of imagined latent rollouts.

technologies.name: MuZero
technologies.tagline: Learn only the parts of the world that matter for predicting value, then plan with tree search over that abstraction.

technologies.name: Meta-World
technologies.tagline: Fifty manipulation tasks in one shared action space, built to ask whether multi-task learning actually transfers.

technologies.name: RLBench
technologies.tagline: The 100-task simulated suite the 3D keyframe-policy line lives on.

technologies.name: PlaNet
technologies.tagline: Plan in a learned latent space instead of in pixels, with the recurrent state-space model that everything after it uses.

technologies.name: RoboTurk
technologies.tagline: Crowdsource teleoperation through a phone browser and collect in days what a lab collects in months.

technologies.name: Dactyl
technologies.tagline: A 24-DoF hand reorienting a block, trained entirely in simulation and transferred with zero real-world data.

technologies.name: QT-Opt
technologies.tagline: 580,000 real grasp attempts across a robot farm, producing closed-loop grasping that learned to reposition and retry.

technologies.name: World Models
technologies.tagline: The paper that named the idea: compress the world into a latent model, then train the policy entirely inside it.

technologies.name: SAC
technologies.tagline: Maximum-entropy off-policy RL: sample-efficient enough to run on a real robot.

technologies.name: PPO
technologies.tagline: The clipped-objective policy gradient that made deep RL boring enough to actually use.

technologies.name: Transformer
technologies.tagline: The architecture underneath essentially every robot brain on this map.

technologies.name: Domain Randomization
technologies.tagline: If the simulator is varied enough, reality looks like just another random sample.

technologies.name: GAIL
technologies.tagline: Match the expert's state-action distribution with a discriminator instead of recovering a reward function.

technologies.name: MuJoCo
technologies.tagline: The contact simulator that made continuous-control research possible, later acquired by DeepMind and released free.

technologies.name: DAgger
technologies.tagline: The formal diagnosis and cure for imitation learning's compounding-error problem.

technologies.name: ALVINN
technologies.full_name: Autonomous Land Vehicle In a Neural Network
technologies.tagline: The original end-to-end sensorimotor neural network: pixels in, steering out, 1989.
